findings.title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix so the guard is never invoked
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers decides whether to include an attribute by calling `include_#{attribute}?` (with a trailing question mark). The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no `?`), so it is never called by the serializer framework. The intended check — only serialize website_name when the website is present — does not run, and website_name is serialized unconditionally (yielding a null key when no website is set, unlike every other guarded attribute in this serializer). Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name is not registered as an untrusted attribute, leaking TL0 profile data
findings.body: `website`, `location`, `bio_raw`, etc. are listed in `untrusted_attributes` so they are hidden when a TL0 user is viewed by anonymous visitors (scope.restrict_user_fields?). The new `website_name` attribute is derived directly from `website` but was not added to that list, so the domain/path of a TL0 user's website is serialized to anonymous users even though `website` itself is suppressed. This defeats the existing privacy control. The spec's `untrusted_attributes` list (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb line 11) also wasn't updated, so the 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' test does not cover the new leak.

findings.title: website_name drops query strings and uses bare rescue on URI parsing
findings.body: When the domains match, the returned website_name is `host + URI(website).path`, discarding any query string or fragment from the user's URL (e.g. `example.com/page?id=3` becomes `example.com/page`). The PR description says 'show complete URL path', so this silently truncates URLs. Additionally, `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` swallows all exceptions from malformed URLs; while this returns nil for blanks, a blanket rescue hides unexpected errors — an explicit presence/parse check would be safer.
